The realization request A04's resolved game implies, answered. Every value here is either a member of the permitted set the knowledge narrowed to, or the single member of the authored bound. Nothing invents a quantity, and each `because` says why this value rather than another. This file is a REALIZER's input, not knowledge: none of it is authored, and the realization record keeps it separate from what was derived. UPDATED 30 September: the instantiation for GF2-09.a was removed. That claim asserts at least one objective exists, and GF2-08.a is an established objective on the same collection — so the claim was already satisfied and instantiating another produced a second objective carrying nothing the first did not. Realization now records it as satisfied by the established member instead. 2 October: the WIDEZONE-08.d choice was removed. Under ruling C33 that item is a property statement on S4 and no longer establishes a region, so it has no S5 line to choose a position for. 6 October: a choice for `game::PS1` was added. The Soccer Sport Profile establishes the possession relationship as a bounds-only contribution over the participating opposing teams, which makes the line an authorized free choice rather than a resolved value — so realization now owes an initial holder and this file supplies one. The profile does not author a team and neither does this: the value names one of two indiscernible established teams, and the `because` says why that is a choice rather than an inference. 

PRUNED 2026-10-08: the two Wide Zone channel-extent choices were removed because A04 no longer selects Wide Zone Advantage at all. The new attacking-duel signal group (J_attacking_duel) resolves A04 to a matched package whose constraints are goalkeeper-included-condition, support-lane-requirement, final-third-value and progression-bonus -- none of them contracted -- so the resolved game is GF2 plus the Soccer Sport Profile. The channels the pruned choices sized do not exist in it. Nothing about the held Wide Zone questions is settled by this; the object is simply not part of A04 any more. 

REWRITTEN 2026-10-09 for the directional arrangement (ruling C42). The shared target GF2-03.a no longer exists -- it and the objective that referenced it are retired, preserved in contracts.json -- so its two choices are replaced by four, one noun and one across-extent for each of the two opposing targets. The values are unchanged from what the single target used; what changed is that there are two of them. The teams are not named here: which team takes which end is a setup decision the activity asks the coach to make, exactly as it already asks who starts with the ball. 

REDUCED 2026-10-13 to the four entries that are decisions. The two across-extent entries (`...GF2-03.e::S6` and `...GF2-03.f::S6`) were removed because neither was ever a choice: the authored bound on each line has exactly one member, any other value is refused, and their own reasons said so ("Full width, as authored"). A line like that is now closed by rule -- a justified default, `ONLY_MEMBER_OF_AUTHORED_BOUND`, produced in `back/src/system/realization/justified-defaults.ts` and recorded in the realization record as a default rather than as something somebody chose. The values in the game are unchanged. What stays here is what a rule may NOT close: the two targets' noun and the scoring kind are design alternatives (a line or a zone; which event scores), and who starts with the ball is the coach's. Christian, 13 October: defaults are welcome "provided they don't silently override important learning-design choices". CORRECTED in review, 13 October: "any other value is refused" is a statement about the REALIZER, not about the knowledge. The one member on each of those two lines comes from GF2-05.b, which is authored SUPPORTING / PREFERRED_DEFAULT -- a preferred default, not a requirement. It is the only value authored for the line and realization holds a value to the authored set, so nothing else realizes today; the default's recorded reason now says it is a preferred default rather than "the only value the knowledge permits". Whether a coach may depart from a non-numeric preferred default is an open question for Christian and is not settled by this file. 

ADDED 15 October 2026 (stage K2): `designationBindings`, which of the two instantiated teams holds each end assignment of ruling C42 (TEAM_AT_AXIS_START, TEAM_AT_AXIS_END). His M2 of 17 October asks for the 20 September designation rule, AM-01 ("Use the game's transitions/episode context to resolve contextual team designations."), and a designation fixed at setup is resolved by which team it was assigned to. That assignment is a governed symmetric choice (SD-39), exactly as the initial possession holder above is: the two teams are indiscernible, swapping the two bindings would leave the game identical, and the coach still chooses which physical group takes which end. It is NOT the `designation` property removed on 2 October: nothing is placed on a team, no register row is filled, no role is named, and realization records the binding beside the game rather than in it (realize.ts checks each handle is a member of this game, and that the two ends are held by different teams). Nothing in a game built from the possession game form reads it today, so no activity changes; it is what lets a fact authored for one end's team reach that team and not the other.

choices.because: The near-end target is a line, chosen from the two the knowledge permits (zone or line), for the same reason the single shared target was: a line is the thinner commitment and a coach can mark it with cones in seconds. Both targets take the same noun so the two ends are symmetrical.
The far-end target is a line, matching the near-end one so neither end is easier to score at than the other.
one of the two kinds the selection narrowed to. line_crossed is consistent with the target realized as a line; target_zone_entered would contradict the S3 choice.

The initial holder of possession is a governed free choice, not knowledge: the Soccer Sport Profile bounds the relationship over the participating opposing teams and deliberately names no team, and SD-39 carries the choice. Either of the two established teams is a legitimate value, and the choice is arbitrary BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by neglect — the two members are indiscernible, which is precisely why which one starts cannot be derived and has to be chosen. Naming one handle commits to nothing about it: no football meaning is read into the ordinal, nothing downstream recovers instantiation order from it, and swapping the two would leave the game identical. Recorded against a qualitative bound, so it is reported as unverified rather than as checked (SD-15). CORRECTED 6 October: this was recorded as `#0`, and the realizer mints member handles from 1, so it named no team at all. It passed because the bound is qualitative -- boundCheck is UNVERIFIABLE_QUALITATIVE_BOUND, so nothing compared the value to the instantiated members -- and nothing reads `possession.team` yet. `realize()` now refuses a chosen value that has a handle shape and names no member, so this cannot recur silently. SINCE 13 October the register's declared domain for this row (`fillableFrom: performers.teams[]`) is enforced as well: the value must be a member of that collection as the game holds it, so it IS now compared with the game's teams and is recorded as WITHIN_DECLARED_DOMAIN rather than as unverified. The authored term itself is still a term in words. The decision remains the coach's: the activity tells them to pick, and the recorded handle stands in for that.

No replacement is inferred.

designationBindings.because: Which team takes the axis-start end is a governed symmetric choice (SD-39; ruling C42 assigns the ends at setup and fixes them for the activity), not knowledge. The two established teams are indiscernible, so either is a legitimate value and the choice is arbitrary by construction: naming handle #1 commits to nothing about it, no meaning is read into the ordinal, and swapping the two bindings would leave the game identical. The coach still decides which physical group takes which end.
The counterpart: the other established team takes the far end, because ruling C42 assigns the two teams to opposite ends and a team holds one end.
